body.statement: Given the exact rational matrices \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_L\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), a Turing-model algorithm computes a rational certificate \((\widehat q,\widehat t,\widehat X,\widehat s)\) satisfying \(\texttt{def:rational-gap-certificate}\) in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Exact rational arithmetic verifies the simplex, trace, rule inequalities, and positive-semidefinite constraints, and weak duality certifies \(B^2\widehat s\le V^\star\le B^2\widehat t\) with gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
body.justification: The certificate makes near-optimal rule mixing archivable without claiming an exact real-algebraic optimizer.
body.gap: Kallus establishes the role of randomization and Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong use semidefinite minimax design, but neither produces this exact WRI and RDIM rational risk-gap certificate.
body.consumer: A trial team can select or mix prespecified AWRI rules and independently audit the worst-case risk gap before assignment.
